Figure 03 reaches nine days and 348 miles in treadmill endurance test

Brett Adcock reports 1.2 million steps, without disclosing the power arrangement or a maintenance log.

Humanoids Daily ↗19 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

The reported milestone

Figure founder Brett Adcock said on October 19 that a Figure 03 had walked on a treadmill for nine days, covering 348 miles, approximately 560 kilometres, and 1.2 million steps. The test was still running when he posted. These are company-reported figures rather than an independent certification.

Repeated motion as a hardware test

Repeating a walking cycle in controlled conditions can expose failures that a short demonstration misses. Adcock described the exercise as a side project intended to stress the robot for failures. It examines locomotion, a different activity from the company’s previously reported 200-hour package-sorting test.

What nine days does not establish

The update does not disclose the power arrangement, breaks, maintenance or intervention history. It therefore cannot establish nine days on one battery charge or reliability across factory tasks. The treadmill result concerns a specific controlled setting; performance at customer sites still needs separate evaluation.
